request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Admission: April 30, 2020
Date of Discharge: May 21, 2020

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the GHESKIO MDR-TB hospital on April 30, 2020, with persistent fever, cough, and weight loss. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 and transferred to a separate building to prevent the spread of the virus. The patient did not require oxygen therapy and recovered from COVID-19 three weeks following diagnosis. He was continued on antituberculous therapy without complication.

Medical History:
The patient presented with a history of chronic cough, fever, and weight loss. He was evaluated by the medical staff with a physical examination, chest radiograph, and sputum analysis. The chest radiograph demonstrated a large right upper lobe cavity, with right middle lobe opacity and right hilar fullness. The GeneXpert sputum test was positive for the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with probable resistance to rifampin. The patient was lost to follow-up before hospitalization and initiation of therapy.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up:
The patient is advised to continue regular follow-up with his healthcare provider. He is instructed to complete the prescribed antituberculous therapy and to maximize precautions against COVID-19 to prevent further spread.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in stable condition. He was advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider and to continue antituberculous therapy as prescribed.

Discharge Medications:
Antituberculous regimen composed of bedaquiline, levofloxacin, linezolid, clofazimine, and pyrazinimide was initiated and continued throughout hospitalization.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider. He should continue the prescribed antituberculous therapy and maximize precautions against COVID-19 to prevent further spread.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The patient was admitted to an MDR-TB hospital with pulmonary tuberculosis that probably resists rifampin. He was found to have COVID-19 during the stay. The principal diagnosis is the condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the admission. Here that is the tuberculosis, since the admission was to the MDR-TB hospital and treatment with antituberculous therapy continued throughout. COVID-19 was a mild comorbidity that arose or was diagnosed during the stay.

Tuberculosis codes in ICD-10-AM sit in A15-A19. A15 covers respiratory tuberculosis, bacteriologically and histologically confirmed. Here the GeneXpert sputum test was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, so the diagnosis is bacteriologically confirmed, which places it in A15. The drug resistance is coded with an additional code (Z16.-), so it does not change the three-character category.

CODE: A15
